couplets.gloss: Being truthful means saying only what does no harm to anyone, not merely what is factually accurate.

edges.reason: Answers its own question: truth is speech with no trace of harm in it.
edges.quote: speech with no harm in it at all

edges.reason: Gives someone weighing their words a single test: would saying this do any harm?
edges.quote: no harm in it at all

couplets.gloss: A lie can count as truth if it does nothing but good, as when it saves an innocent person from harm.

edges.reason: Stretches truthfulness to cover even a lie, so long as the good it brings has no fault in it.
edges.quote: Even a lie counts as truthfulness

edges.reason: Sets the bar for a lie very high: the good it brings must be free of all fault.
edges.quote: if it brings good with no fault in it

couplets.gloss: Never lie about what you know in your heart to be so: once you have, your own mind will torment you.

edges.reason: Makes the liar their own punisher, burned from within once the lie is told.
edges.quote: your own heart will burn you

edges.reason: Warns anyone about to lie that their own heart will burn them for it afterwards.
edges.quote: Don’t lie about what your own heart knows

couplets.gloss: Someone who is honest right through, not just in words, earns a place in everyone's heart.

edges.reason: Promises anyone who lives without lying a place in every heart.
edges.quote: you will live in the hearts of all the world

couplets.gloss: A person who speaks the truth from the heart outranks both those who fast and those who give to charity.

edges.reason: Ranks a heart set on truth above both penance and almsgiving.
edges.quote: you stand above those who practise penance and give alms

couplets.gloss: No reputation beats being known as someone who never lies, and that brings every good thing without any hardship.

edges.reason: Its reward needs no toil: not lying is enough to bring all righteousness.
edges.quote: Without any toil, it gives you all righteousness

couplets.gloss: If you can go through life without ever lying, you hardly need any other virtue.

edges.reason: Treats a life with no lie in it as enough, leaving other righteous deeds nothing to add.
edges.quote: leave other righteous deeds undone

couplets.gloss: Water cleans the outside of you, but only honesty shows that you are clean on the inside.

edges.reason: Gives the test of an inner purity that water can’t reach: is this person truthful?
edges.quote: Inner purity is seen through truthfulness

edges.reason: Sets truthfulness to do for the inside what water does for the outside.
edges.quote: seen through truthfulness

couplets.gloss: Good people don't count ordinary lamps as real light: honesty is the one lamp that deserves the name.

edges.reason: Among all lamps, the worthy give the name of lamp to not lying and nothing else.
edges.quote: To the worthy, the only lamp is the lamp of not lying

edges.reason: Sets not lying beside every other lamp and finds it the only true one.
edges.quote: the lamp of not lying

couplets.gloss: Of everything the poet has witnessed in life, nothing is better than truth.

edges.reason: Of all the poet has seen to be true, nothing stands higher than truthfulness.
edges.quote: nothing at all is better than truthfulness

couplets.gloss: Restraining your temper only means something when you could really do harm; if you can't, it proves nothing.

edges.reason: Holding back only means something where your anger could take effect.
edges.quote: holds back anger where it can take effect

edges.reason: Anger held in where it could do damage is the only restraint that counts.
edges.quote: what does it matter if you hold it back or not

couplets.gloss: Anger is wrong even when you can't act on it, and when you can act on it nothing is worse.
couplets.sensitive: calls anger wrong even in someone helpless

edges.reason: Leaves anger no excuse: bad where it can’t take effect, and at its worst where it can.
edges.quote: Anger is bad where it can’t take effect

edges.reason: Someone whose anger can take effect on others is told that nothing is worse.
edges.quote: Where it can, nothing is worse

couplets.gloss: Let go of your anger at anyone at all, whoever they are, because it only breeds more harm.
couplets.sensitive: tells the wronged to drop anger at any offender

edges.reason: Allows no exception for anyone, since evil things are born of anger.
edges.quote: Evil things are born of it

edges.reason: Speaks straight to the person with a grievance: whoever did it, put the anger down.
edges.quote: Forget your anger, whoever it is against

couplets.gloss: Anger kills laughter and joy: no enemy does you more damage.

edges.reason: Counts what it kills, the smile and the joy, and finds no other enemy to match it.
edges.quote: What other enemy is there

couplets.gloss: If you care about yourself, stay away from rage, because left unchecked it will destroy you first.

edges.reason: Turns anger back on its owner: left unguarded, the one it kills is you.
edges.quote: it is you that anger kills

edges.reason: Asks the angry person to put their own safety first and step back from the rage.
edges.quote: If you would guard yourself, guard against anger

couplets.gloss: Anger destroys anyone who goes near it and burns up the family that could have been their lifeline.

edges.reason: Says the damage spreads past the angry person to the people who keep them safe.
edges.quote: burns the raft of safety that is your own people

edges.reason: Anger acts as a fire here, killing whoever comes near it and burning your own people too.
edges.quote: the killer of those who come near it, burns

edges.reason: Calls your own people a raft of safety, and anger is what burns it.
edges.quote: the raft of safety

couplets.gloss: Treating your rage as something to treasure is like punching the floor: you are certain to get hurt.

edges.reason: Pictures prized anger as a blow struck on the ground, with ruin as certain for the one who strikes.
edges.quote: a hand that strikes the ground can’t escape

couplets.gloss: Even when people hurt you as badly as being plunged into fire, it is best if you can keep from getting angry.
couplets.sensitive: urges no anger even under severe mistreatment

edges.reason: Holds the ideal at its limit: no anger, though the wrongs are past bearing.
edges.quote: it is good not to be angry, if you can

edges.reason: Meets a person at the height of their hurt and still asks them to hold off.
edges.quote: Even if someone hurts you as a mass of flame would

edges.reason: Measures the pain of being wronged against standing in a mass of flames.
edges.quote: as a mass of flame would

couplets.gloss: Drive anger out of your mind completely and everything you hope for will come to you at once.

edges.reason: Promises every wish, at once, to the person who has cleared anger from the heart.
edges.quote: never even think of anger in your heart

couplets.gloss: People consumed by rage are as good as dead, while those who give it up are equal to those who have renounced the world.

edges.reason: Divides people by it: those far gone in anger are like the dead, and those who renounce it equal the renouncers.
edges.quote: Those who renounce anger are the equals of renouncers

edges.reason: Someone far gone in anger still breathes but is counted among the dead.
edges.quote: Those far gone in anger are like the dead

couplets.gloss: Good people won't hurt anyone, even if doing so would make them rich and honoured.

edges.reason: Keeps the rule even with wealth and high standing as the prize for breaking it.
edges.quote: Doing no harm to others, even for wealth that brings high standing

couplets.gloss: Even when someone hurts them out of hatred, good people do not hurt them back.
couplets.sensitive: counsels not answering injury done in hate

edges.reason: Holds the rule against the hardest case, harm done in hatred.
edges.quote: even when someone has harmed you in hatred

edges.reason: Makes refusing to harm in return the settled rule of the stainless, whatever was done to them.
edges.quote: Not harming in return

couplets.gloss: Hurting someone, even a person who attacked you for no reason, brings you trouble you will never recover from.
couplets.sensitive: warns an unprovoked victim against hitting back

edges.reason: Extends the ban to one who hated you without cause.
edges.quote: those who hated you when you had done nothing to them

edges.reason: Puts the cost of paying back on the one who does it: misery that can’t be escaped.
edges.quote: misery you can’t escape

couplets.gloss: The best way to punish people who hurt you is to treat them well and leave them ashamed.
couplets.sensitive: tells the injured to repay harm with kindness

edges.reason: Turns the question of punishment into an instruction to do the offender a good turn.
edges.quote: do them such good that they are ashamed

edges.reason: Replaces payback with a kindness, so that shame is the only penalty left.
edges.quote: such good that they are ashamed

edges.reason: Answers someone asking how to get back at an offender: do them good and let them feel it.
edges.quote: The way to punish those who harm you

couplets.gloss: What good is being clever if you don't treat another creature's pain as your own and avoid causing it?

edges.reason: Rates understanding as useless unless it guards against another’s pain as its own.
edges.quote: guard against another’s pain as you would your own

couplets.gloss: Once you know how something hurts, make sure you never do it to anyone else.

edges.reason: Turns what you know of pain into a rule: don’t do it to anyone else.
edges.quote: you must not do to anyone else

couplets.gloss: The highest thing is never to hurt anyone deliberately, at any time or to any degree.

edges.reason: Leaves no gap in the rule: no person, no moment and no degree of harm is excepted.
edges.quote: Doing no wilful harm, in any measure, at any time, to anyone

couplets.gloss: How can anyone who knows what suffering feels like go on making other creatures suffer?

edges.reason: Asks in disbelief how anyone who knows harm firsthand can do it to others.
edges.quote: Why, then, do you harm other lives

couplets.gloss: Harm someone in the morning and by the afternoon the harm will come back to you by itself.

edges.reason: Compresses the return of a deed into one day: harm in the morning, harm in the afternoon.
edges.quote: harm will come to you in the afternoon, by itself

edges.reason: Gives a blunt reason to hurt no one: the harm needs no help to come home.
edges.quote: Harm others in the morning

couplets.gloss: All the harm people do ends up falling on them, so those who want a life free of pain avoid doing harm.

edges.reason: States the law at its widest: all pain falls back on the one who caused it.
edges.quote: All pain falls on those who cause pain

edges.reason: Argues from self-interest: refrain from harm if you would live untouched by it.
edges.quote: Those who want to be free of pain cause none

couplets.gloss: Not killing is the highest virtue, because killing brings every other wrong along with it.

edges.reason: Names not killing as righteous action itself, because killing brings every action of the other kind.
edges.quote: What is righteous action? Not killing

couplets.gloss: Sharing your food and protecting living creatures is the highest of all the duties religious teachers have laid down.

edges.reason: Makes sharing your food one half of the highest thing the learned have gathered.
edges.quote: Sharing your food

edges.reason: Places caring for living things beside sharing food, first among all the learned have gathered.
edges.quote: caring for many living things

couplets.gloss: Not killing comes first among all goods, and not lying comes right after it.

edges.reason: Gives it first place outright, with no rival beside it.
edges.quote: Not killing stands alone as good

edges.reason: Honours not lying with the only place left, next after not killing.
edges.quote: Next after it, not lying is good

couplets.gloss: The right path is the one that always asks how to avoid killing anything, even the smallest creature.

edges.reason: Measures the good path by its care to kill nothing at all.
edges.quote: takes care to kill nothing at all

couplets.gloss: Of all who have renounced the world, the greatest is the one who shrinks from killing and honours all life.

edges.reason: Ranks highest the renouncer who dreads killing and keeps to not killing.
edges.quote: the highest is the one who dreads killing

edges.reason: Judges among those who have already given up the world and ranks one of them first.
edges.quote: Among all who dread the state they are in and renounce

couplets.gloss: Death, which devours every life, stays away from the days of someone who lives by a vow not to kill.

edges.reason: Holds out the rarest reward for not killing: days that death leaves alone.
edges.quote: someone who holds to not killing

edges.reason: Death is an eater of lives who won’t come upon this person’s days.
edges.quote: Death, which eats lives

couplets.gloss: Never take another creature's life, which is as sweet to it as yours is to you, even to save your own.
couplets.sensitive: counsels dying rather than killing, even to survive

edges.reason: Binds the rule even where the price of keeping it is one's own life.
edges.quote: Even if you lose your own life for it

couplets.gloss: However great the gains from killing may be, good people regard them as the lowest kind of gain.

edges.reason: Rejects any gain won by killing, however great it may be.
edges.quote: gain that comes from killing is the lowest thing

couplets.gloss: Those who make a living by killing are held by people of judgement to be as low as those who feed on rotting flesh.
couplets.sensitive: the Tamil ranks killers with low-caste work

edges.reason: Shows the contempt a living made by killing earns from those who can see baseness.
edges.quote: People who live by killing

couplets.gloss: The wise say that people living with terrible sores and misery must have taken lives in a previous existence.
couplets.sensitive: blames the sick for their disease

edges.reason: Has people trace a diseased body to lives taken before, a deed coming home in the flesh.
edges.quote: are those who took life from bodies

edges.reason: Reads a diseased body as the price of taking life, which warns against it.
edges.quote: took life from bodies

couplets.gloss: The worst kind of stupidity is mistaking what passes away for something that will last.

edges.reason: Ranks taking the passing for the lasting as the lowest error of all.
edges.quote: takes what doesn’t last for what lasts

couplets.gloss: Great wealth arrives like a crowd gathering for a show and leaves the same way when the show ends.

edges.reason: Wealth gathers and scatters as a crowd at a dance does, with nothing to hold it.
edges.quote: It goes the way that crowd goes when the dance is over

couplets.gloss: Wealth never stays, so when you have it, use it at once for something that lasts.

edges.reason: Opens on the plain fact that wealth doesn’t stay.
edges.quote: It is the nature of wealth not to stay

edges.reason: The things that stay, which it says to do at once, can only be good deeds, since wealth won’t wait.
edges.quote: do at once the things that stay

couplets.gloss: A day seems harmless, but to those who understand, it is a blade cutting steadily through your life.

edges.reason: Unmasks the harmless-looking passage of days as a blade that never stops cutting.
edges.quote: a blade sawing through life

couplets.gloss: Hurry to do good before your tongue locks and the death rattle starts.

edges.reason: Presses for good deeds now, with the stilled tongue as the deadline.
edges.quote: rush to do good deeds

edges.reason: Whoever keeps postponing the good they mean to do is shown the last deadline there is.
edges.quote: Before your tongue is stilled and the hiccup rises

edges.reason: Turns the thought of dying into a plain instruction: do good while you still can.
edges.quote: rush to do good deeds

couplets.gloss: Someone is here yesterday and gone today: that is the strange marvel of this world.

edges.reason: With grim irony, names as the world’s greatness that a man here yesterday is gone today.
edges.quote: a man was here yesterday and is gone today

couplets.gloss: People can't be sure of the next minute, yet they carry around millions of plans.

edges.reason: Life's hold is so thin that no one can vouch for the coming minute.
edges.quote: can’t be sure of living one moment more

edges.reason: Puts all one's schemes in proportion for anyone shaken by how uncertain life is.
edges.quote: they think thoughts by the ten million

couplets.gloss: The bond between soul and body is like a chick leaving its broken shell behind and flying off.

edges.reason: The soul is the bird that flies, and the body the egg left lying alone.
edges.quote: a bird that flies off and leaves the egg lying alone

edges.reason: Aiyar's love of soul for body lasts only until the bird flies, so the tie is a passing one.
edges.quote: the love between the soul and the body

couplets.gloss: Death is like falling asleep, and being born again is like waking up afterwards.
couplets.sensitive: likens death to sleep, which a despairing reader may take as comfort

edges.reason: Each birth is a waking from the sleep of death.
edges.quote: Birth is like waking after sleep

couplets.gloss: Does the soul have no real home, that it has to take shelter in this poor body?

edges.reason: Treats the body as a makeshift shelter for a soul with no house of its own.
edges.quote: Has it still found no home of its own

couplets.gloss: Whatever you let go of can no longer cause you pain.

edges.reason: Promises relief item by item: each thing given up takes its own pain with it.
edges.quote: From each thing you have let go of, you suffer no more pain

edges.reason: Tells someone drawn to letting go that every single thing dropped is a sorrow escaped.
edges.quote: each thing you have let go of

couplets.gloss: If you want happiness, give things up while you still have them: many joys come after you do.

edges.reason: Reverses the expected loss: renouncing brings many things here, rather than taking them away.
edges.quote: Once you have renounced, many things are yours here

edges.reason: Adds urgency for one already feeling the pull: if you want what it brings, go while you can.
edges.quote: renounce while you can

couplets.gloss: Subdue all five senses and give up, all at once, everything you enjoy.

edges.reason: Demands in so many words that the five senses be crushed.
edges.quote: crush the hold of the five senses

edges.reason: Asks for more than the senses: everything you wanted is to go, all together.
edges.quote: give up, all together, everything you wanted

couplets.gloss: Owning nothing is the natural rule for someone under vows: keeping even one thing draws them back into the trap.

edges.reason: States the rule of the renouncer in one line: to have nothing at all.
edges.quote: Having nothing at all is the way of penance

edges.reason: Speaks of one doing penance, warning that owning a single thing brings back delusion.
edges.quote: Owning even one thing brings back delusion

couplets.gloss: For someone trying to end the cycle of rebirth your own flesh is excess baggage, so why keep any other ties?

edges.reason: Argues up from the body itself: if that is too much, every lesser tie is worse.
edges.quote: even the body is too much

couplets.gloss: The ego's sense of me and my things is pure pride: whoever cuts it away reaches a world above the gods.

edges.reason: Traces pride to the very words “I” and “mine”, and promises a higher world for cutting it away.
edges.quote: the pride that says “I” and “mine”

couplets.gloss: Those who cling to things and won't let go are themselves gripped by suffering that won't let go.

edges.reason: Mirrors clinging with its punishment: they won’t let go, and suffering won’t let go of them.
edges.quote: hold on to attachment and won’t let go

couplets.gloss: Those who give up everything are on their way to freedom; everyone else is confused and caught in a net.

edges.reason: Allows no middle ground: complete renouncing arrives, and all others sit in a net.
edges.quote: Those who renounce completely have arrived

couplets.gloss: The moment you are free of attachment, rebirth ends; until then you only go on in what cannot last.

edges.reason: Says that without ending attachment you go on seeing impermanence.
edges.quote: Otherwise you will see impermanence

edges.reason: Fixes the exact moment of freedom: birth is cut off the instant attachment ends.
edges.quote: The moment attachment ends, birth is cut off

couplets.gloss: Hold on to God, who has no attachments; hold on to that so that you can let go of everything else.

edges.reason: Bids the seeker hold to the one who has no attachment.
edges.quote: Hold to the attachment of the one who has no attachment

edges.reason: Makes letting go of attachment the reason for holding to that one.
edges.quote: so that you can let go of attachment

edges.reason: Aiyar's ark is the refuge one grips to be carried free, though the Tamil only says cling.
edges.quote: hold fast to that ark

couplets.gloss: Taking worthless things for what truly matters is the mistake that gives you a wretched life.

edges.reason: Blames a wretched birth on one error, taking what isn’t real for what is.
edges.quote: the delusion that takes what isn’t real for what is

couplets.gloss: Once confusion lifts and you see clearly, the darkness is gone and joy takes its place.

edges.reason: Shows what its removal yields: those rid of it get joy in place of darkness.
edges.quote: have left delusion behind

edges.reason: Credits stainless seeing with bringing joy to the one who has it.
edges.quote: see without stain

edges.reason: Error is a darkness here, and it lifts for the one who sees clearly.
edges.quote: darkness goes and joy comes

couplets.gloss: Someone who has moved past doubt and found what is real stands closer to heaven than to the ground under their feet.

edges.reason: Puts heaven nearer than earth for those whose doubts have ended.
edges.quote: heaven is nearer than the earth

couplets.gloss: Even with all your human faculties, nothing is gained if you never grasp what is real.

edges.reason: Counts even mastery of the senses as no gain without knowledge of the truth.
edges.quote: no gain in it without knowledge of the truth

couplets.gloss: Real wisdom means seeing what a thing truly is, whatever it appears to be.

edges.reason: Names the work of understanding as finding the true in every thing, whatever form it takes.
edges.quote: understanding is seeing the reality in it

couplets.gloss: Those who study deeply and find the truth here set out on the road that does not lead back to this world.

edges.reason: Joins learning to insight and rewards the pair with a path that doesn’t come back.
edges.quote: Those who learn here and see the truth

edges.reason: Makes the path with no return to this world the prize held out.
edges.quote: the path that doesn’t come back here

couplets.gloss: Once your mind has reflected and truly grasped what is real, you need no longer think about being born again.

edges.reason: Relieves the one who has reasoned their way to what truly is of all thought of another birth.
edges.quote: you need not think of being born again

couplets.gloss: Wisdom is seeing the highest good, so that you are rid of the foolishness of being born.

edges.reason: Gives understanding its aim: to see the pure reality called excellence.
edges.quote: see the pure reality called excellence

edges.reason: Birth itself is the folly here, and ending it is what understanding aims at.
edges.quote: the folly called birth

couplets.gloss: If you know what your freedom rests on and live so as to break your attachments, the troubles ahead of you will leave.

edges.reason: Treats living so that attachment dies as what sends future ills away.
edges.quote: live so that attachment dies

edges.reason: Knowing what to rest on is this insight, and it comes before the living.
edges.quote: If you know what to rest on

couplets.gloss: When desire, anger and confusion fade, even their very names, your troubles fade away with them.

edges.reason: Heads the three whose going takes pain along with it.
edges.quote: desire

edges.reason: Stands between desire and delusion among the three whose names must go for pain to go.
edges.quote: anger

edges.reason: Closes the list of three, the mistaking of things that goes with wanting and rage.
edges.quote: delusion

couplets.gloss: Desire is what every living being's endless births grow from, at all times.

edges.reason: Says what craving is at bottom: the seed from which every life’s births are grown.
edges.quote: craving is the seed

edges.reason: Birth is what never ends, and craving is the seed it grows from.
edges.quote: the seed that yields

couplets.gloss: If you must want something, want never to be reborn, and you will get that by wanting to stop wanting.

edges.reason: Names it the one longing worth having, if one must long at all.
edges.quote: want not to be born

edges.reason: Gives the paradox: what opens the way is wanting to want nothing.
edges.quote: wanting to want nothing

couplets.gloss: Nothing here or anywhere else is as valuable as wanting nothing.

edges.reason: No wealth here, and nothing anywhere else, comes up to it.
edges.quote: no great wealth here to match wanting nothing

edges.reason: Takes the word wealth from money and hands it to the state of wanting nothing.
edges.quote: no great wealth here

couplets.gloss: Being pure just means being free of desire, and you get there by wanting truth above everything.

edges.reason: Reduces purity to one thing, having no craving left.
edges.quote: Purity is having no craving

couplets.gloss: The truly free are those who have lost their desires; anyone else may look free but is still tied down.

edges.reason: Keeps the name of free for those rid of craving and denies it to the rest.
edges.quote: Those who are called free are the ones free of craving

edges.reason: Shows everyone else as not free in the same way, for lack of it.
edges.quote: The others are not free in the same way

couplets.gloss: If you care about doing right, run from desire, because desire is what tricks you.

edges.reason: Warns that craving is what deceives you.
edges.quote: Craving is what deceives you

couplets.gloss: Cut out your desires completely and liberation will come however you choose to seek it.

edges.reason: Says that with craving wholly cut away, deeds that never fail come as you want them.
edges.quote: cut off craving completely

couplets.gloss: With no desires you have no sorrow; if you do have them, one misery follows another.

edges.reason: Piles suffering on suffering upon whoever goes on craving.
edges.quote: suffering comes on and on, without end

edges.reason: Shows a person always after the next thing that the wanting itself feeds the misery.
edges.quote: Those without craving have no suffering

couplets.gloss: Get rid of desire, the worst misery there is, and you will have unbroken joy even in this life.

edges.reason: Calls it outright the worst suffering of all.
edges.quote: craving, the worst suffering of all

edges.reason: Offers unbroken joy, and not later but here, to whoever destroys craving.
edges.quote: joy goes on unbroken, even here

couplets.gloss: Desire can never be satisfied, but the moment you give it up you reach a state that never changes.

edges.reason: Declares it a hunger that no getting can ever fill.
edges.quote: whose nature is never to be filled

edges.reason: Tells someone stuck chasing more that satisfaction lies in stopping, not in the next gain.
edges.quote: If you give up craving

couplets.gloss: The best ruler is one who has all six: an army, a people, resources, advisers, allies and defences.

edges.reason: Measures rulers against each other and says who stands as the bull among them.
edges.quote: a bull among rulers

edges.reason: Sets out the six possessions by which a ruler's standing is judged.
edges.quote: whoever has all six

edges.reason: The army stands first in the list of six.
edges.quote: An army

edges.reason: Food, the crop that is the realm’s wealth, comes third.
edges.quote: food

edges.reason: Friends, the Tamil’s நட்பு, come fifth.
edges.quote: friends

edges.reason: Forts close the list of what such a ruler must hold.
edges.quote: forts

couplets.gloss: A ruler must never run short of these four: courage, generosity, good sense and drive.

edges.reason: Lays down what must never be missing in the ruler himself.
edges.quote: a ruler’s nature is never to lack these four

edges.reason: Names the marks of the office in what a ruler is, not in what he owns.
edges.quote: never to lack these four

edges.reason: Leads the four things a ruler may never lack.
edges.quote: Fearlessness

edges.reason: A ruler’s giving is second among the four that must not fail.
edges.quote: giving

edges.reason: Understanding, the Tamil’s அறிவு, is the good sense a ruler needs third.
edges.quote: understanding

edges.reason: Drive closes the list of what no ruler can go without.
edges.quote: drive

couplets.gloss: People fit to govern a land never lose these three: alertness, education and decisiveness.

edges.reason: Speaks of those who rule the land, not of people in general.
edges.quote: those who rule the land

edges.reason: Marks a ruler by three things that must stay with him for good.
edges.quote: these three never leave

edges.reason: Wakefulness, the Tamil’s not sleeping, opens the three.
edges.quote: Wakefulness

edges.reason: Study is the second thing that may never leave one who rules.
edges.quote: learning

edges.reason: Resolve completes the three: the firmness to settle a matter and hold to it.
edges.quote: resolve

couplets.gloss: A good ruler keeps to what is right, gets rid of wrong, and guards his honour without failing in courage.

edges.reason: Written as a charge, setting out what the ruler shall and shall not do.
edges.quote: A ruler keeps to righteousness

edges.reason: Requires of him first that righteousness never fail and that wrong be removed.
edges.quote: keeps to righteousness, removes what is wrong

edges.reason: Charges him with an honour that never slips.
edges.quote: an honour that never slips from valour

edges.reason: Forbids any lapse in valour, the Tamil's மறன், even as he guards his name.
edges.quote: never slips from valour

couplets.gloss: A competent ruler knows how to build up resources, raise revenue, protect it, and spend it well.

edges.reason: Holds the ruler himself to these four tasks.
edges.quote: A ruler is one who can

edges.reason: Describes the office as four tasks: to create, gather, guard and share out.
edges.quote: create, gather and guard, and share out what is guarded

couplets.gloss: A ruler who is easy to reach and never speaks harshly makes his country respected above all others.

edges.reason: Ties the land’s standing to two habits of its ruler.
edges.quote: his land will be praised above all others

edges.reason: Asks that a ruler be easy for people to see.
edges.quote: easy to see

edges.reason: Names a sharp tongue as the other thing an esteemed ruler must not have.
edges.quote: not harsh in speech

edges.reason: Anyone leading others gets two plain rules: let people reach you, and do not snap at them.
edges.quote: easy to see and not harsh in speech

couplets.gloss: A ruler who gives generously and protects his people with kind words finds the world goes as he says.

edges.reason: Promises one who gives and protects with sweet words a world that follows their word.
edges.quote: the world is just as their own word would have it

edges.reason: Praises giving when it is done with sweet words.
edges.quote: give and protect with sweet words

edges.reason: The gift is to come with sweet words, the Tamil’s இன்சொல்.
edges.quote: with sweet words

couplets.gloss: A ruler who gives fair judgement and protects his people will be treated as a god by them.

edges.reason: Raises the ruler who does justice and protects to the rank of lord of the people.
edges.quote: the lord of his people

edges.reason: Joins the two halves of good rule, even justice and the guarding of the people.
edges.quote: does justice and protects

couplets.gloss: The world happily stays under the rule of a leader who can put up with words that sting.

edges.reason: Says the world will rest under the umbrella of the ruler who can bear this.
edges.quote: The world rests under the umbrella

edges.reason: Calls it a virtue in a ruler to sit still under what is bitter to hear.
edges.quote: bear words bitter to his ears

couplets.gloss: A ruler who is generous, gracious, just and cares for his people shines among rulers.

edges.reason: Holds up the ruler with all these gifts as the brightest of his kind.
edges.quote: a light among rulers

edges.reason: Giving leads the list of what makes a light among rulers.
edges.quote: Giving

edges.reason: The straight sceptre, the Tamil’s செங்கோல், is third of the four.
edges.quote: a straight sceptre

couplets.gloss: Learn thoroughly what is worth learning, and then live by what you have learned.

edges.reason: Is not satisfied with study alone: what is learned must be lived up to.
edges.quote: Once you have learned it, live up to it

couplets.gloss: Mathematics and reading are the two eyes that every living person needs.

edges.reason: Makes numbers and letters the sight of every living person, not a luxury.
edges.quote: What they call numbers and what they call letters

edges.reason: Two branches of knowledge are counted as the pair of eyes one sees the world with.
edges.quote: these two, they say, are the eyes of those who live

couplets.gloss: Only educated people truly have eyes: the uneducated just have two open wounds on their face.

edges.reason: Grants the power of seeing to the learned and no one else.
edges.quote: Those said to have eyes are the learned

edges.reason: Reduces the eyes of the unlearned to a pair of sores.
edges.quote: The unlearned have two sores on their faces

edges.reason: Sets working eyes against sores in the face to show what learning does for a person.
edges.quote: two sores on their faces

couplets.gloss: Scholars make people glad when they arrive and leave people thinking of them when they go.

edges.reason: Describes the way of the learned among others, welcomed and then missed.
edges.quote: that is the way of the learned

edges.reason: Shows its charm in company, where those left behind regret the parting.
edges.quote: to part so that they long to meet again

couplets.gloss: Even if you must stand humbly before a teacher like a pauper before the rich, learn: those who won't are the lowest people.

edges.reason: Finds it worth the humbling of yearning like the poor before the rich.
edges.quote: yearning like the poor before the rich

edges.reason: Ranks those who don’t learn lowest of all.
edges.quote: Those who don’t learn are the lowest

edges.reason: Speaks of the one who learns, who may have to stoop like the poor before the rich.
edges.quote: Some learn, though it means yearning

couplets.gloss: Knowledge is like a spring dug in sand: the more you draw from it, the more it flows.

edges.reason: Promises that understanding, like a well dug in sand, flows as far as you go.
edges.quote: People’s understanding flows as far as they learn

couplets.gloss: An educated person is at home in any town or country, so why would anyone stay unlearned until they die?

edges.reason: Says of the learned alone that no town is foreign to them.
edges.quote: To the learned, every country is their country

edges.reason: Asks why anyone would go to the grave still untaught when the reward is so plain.
edges.quote: Why then does anyone go without learning until they die

couplets.gloss: What you learn in one life keeps lifting you up through all the lives that follow.

edges.reason: Claims for learning a reward that outlives the body and serves through seven births.
edges.quote: shelters you for seven

couplets.gloss: Learned people see that what delights them also delights others, and that makes them love learning even more.

edges.reason: Shows a delight that grows by being shared with the world.
edges.quote: the world delights in what delights them

edges.reason: Looks into the hearts of the learned to find why they keep at it.
edges.quote: the learned desire it all the more

couplets.gloss: Education is the one wealth that never decays or runs out: everything else you own is nothing beside it.

edges.reason: Holds it beyond destruction, where all else counts as no wealth at all.
edges.quote: All else is not wealth

edges.reason: Applies the word wealth to learning and strips it from all else.
edges.quote: Learning is the great wealth that can’t be destroyed

couplets.gloss: Getting up to address a gathering without deep knowledge is like playing a board game with no board.

edges.reason: Without study a speaker has no ground to move on, as counters have none without a board.
edges.quote: without having studied fully

edges.reason: Speaks of the one who holds forth in an assembly, and of what they lack if unread.
edges.quote: Speaking in an assembly

couplets.gloss: An unlearned person wanting to be admired as a speaker wants what he simply doesn't have the means for.
couplets.sensitive: mocks a woman's body to make its point

edges.reason: Ridicules the unlearned man’s wish to speak when he has nothing to speak with.
edges.quote: An unlearned man’s desire to speak

couplets.gloss: Even the uneducated can be thought well of, provided they keep quiet in front of the educated.

edges.reason: Its backhanded praise leaves silence as the only credit open to the unlearned.
edges.quote: if they can keep from speaking in front of the learned

couplets.gloss: Even if an uneducated person says something sensible, knowledgeable people won't accept it.

edges.reason: Shows its cost: without study even a sound view finds no hearing among the wise.
edges.quote: the wise don’t accept it

couplets.gloss: An uneducated person with a high opinion of himself is exposed the moment he speaks in front of others.

edges.reason: Has the unlearned man shamed as soon as he opens his lips in company.
edges.quote: falls away when he comes face to face with others and speaks

edges.reason: The trouble is his belief in his own wisdom, which one speech undoes.
edges.quote: An unlearned man’s standing falls away

couplets.gloss: People who never studied are like barren land: about all you can say for them is that they exist.

edges.reason: Pictures the unlearned as salt land that yields nothing.
edges.quote: salt land that yields nothing

edges.reason: Leaves them nothing but bare existence, alive in name and no more.
edges.quote: All you can say of the unlearned is that they exist

couplets.gloss: Without a sharp, deep mind, good looks are no better than a nicely painted clay doll.

edges.reason: Strips a handsome body of value when the mind behind it has taken in nothing deep.
edges.quote: like those of a well-made clay doll

couplets.gloss: Money owned by the uneducated does more harm than poverty suffered by good people.

edges.reason: Puts wealth with the unlearned below poverty with the good.
edges.quote: Wealth in the hands of the unlearned

couplets.gloss: An uneducated person of high birth counts for less than an educated person of humble birth.

edges.reason: Denies the unlearned any shelter in a high birth.
edges.quote: The unlearned, though born high

edges.reason: Lets learning lift those born low above those born high.
edges.quote: the standing of the learned, though born low

edges.reason: Places the learned by their learning alone, however low their birth.
edges.quote: the learned, though born low

couplets.gloss: The educated are as far above the uneducated as people are above animals.

edges.reason: Sets the distance between learned and unlearned equal to that between humans and beasts.
edges.quote: As beasts are to humans

couplets.gloss: What you gain through listening is the greatest of all riches, above every other kind.

edges.reason: Crowns what is learned by ear above every other kind of wealth.
edges.quote: first among all wealth

edges.reason: Gives the ear a wealth of its own, filled by what it hears.
edges.quote: the wealth of the ear

edges.reason: Takes the highest name for wealth and gives it to the ear.
edges.quote: The wealth of wealth

couplets.gloss: Only when there is nothing left to feed your ears should you give a little to your stomach.

edges.reason: Puts food for the ear ahead of a meal, leaving the stomach to wait its turn.
edges.quote: give the stomach a little too

edges.reason: Treats the ear as a second mouth, served first, with hearing as its food.
edges.quote: food for the ear

couplets.gloss: People who have taken in a great deal of wise teaching are like gods walking the earth.

edges.reason: Makes anyone fed by listening the equal of the gods, here on earth.
edges.quote: the equals of the gods

couplets.gloss: Listen to wise teaching even if you never studied, because it will hold you up when things go badly.

edges.reason: Opens this road even to someone with no learning, as a prop when they falter.
edges.quote: Even if you have no learning, listen

couplets.gloss: Advice from good people is like a strong walking stick: it keeps you upright on slippery ground.

edges.reason: Likens the words of the upright to a firm staff in the hand of one who might slip.
edges.quote: like a staff on slippery ground

couplets.gloss: Listen to good advice even if it's only a little: even a little will raise you by that much.

edges.reason: Assures that no amount is too small, since even that little brings greatness.
edges.quote: Listen to good things, however little

couplets.gloss: People who have listened closely and thought things through don't talk foolishly, even when they've got something wrong.

edges.reason: Credits gathered listening with keeping someone from folly even when mistaken.
edges.quote: Even when they have misunderstood

couplets.gloss: An ear that has never been trained by instruction is deaf, even though it can hear.

edges.reason: Declares hearing without listening to be a kind of deafness.
edges.quote: are deaf, even though they hear

edges.reason: Pictures the ear as something bored through, opened only by listening.
edges.quote: Ears not pierced by listening

couplets.gloss: It is hard for anyone who hasn't listened to subtle teaching to speak with humility.

edges.reason: Makes humble speech a thing out of reach for those who never sat and listened.
edges.quote: Those without subtle listening

couplets.gloss: People who relish food but have no appetite for what the ear can learn make no real difference to anyone.
couplets.sensitive: says some lives make no difference to the world

edges.reason: Says someone with no taste for listening is one the world would hardly notice losing.
edges.quote: what does it matter if they die or live

edges.reason: Gives the ear a palate of its own, set against the tongue that knows only food.
edges.quote: the tastes of the ear

couplets.gloss: Good sense protects you from sudden harm and is a fortress that no enemy can break into.

edges.reason: Gives understanding as a tool against ruin and a fort that no enemy can destroy.
edges.quote: a fort inside that even enemies can’t destroy

couplets.gloss: Good sense stops your mind going wherever it likes, keeps it from harm and steers it toward what's right.

edges.reason: Says what understanding does: it reins in the mind and turns it to the good.
edges.quote: It turns it from evil and guides it to good

couplets.gloss: Wisdom means finding the truth in what is said, no matter who says it.

edges.reason: Its test is sifting any statement on its merits, paying no regard to the speaker.
edges.quote: Whatever you hear, from whoever’s mouth

couplets.gloss: A wise person says hard things in a way everyone can follow, and catches the fine points in what others say.

edges.reason: Credits the wise with two skills of tongue and ear: speaking plainly and catching subtleties.
edges.quote: seeing the subtle meaning in what others say

couplets.gloss: A wise person gets on with everyone and stays level-headed, neither overjoyed nor crushed.

edges.reason: Gives understanding an even temper that neither blooms nor closes.
edges.quote: Not to bloom and then close is understanding

couplets.gloss: Part of being wise is living the way the world around you lives.

edges.reason: Counts moving in step with the world as part of understanding itself.
edges.quote: understanding is living that way with the world

couplets.gloss: Sensible people can tell what's coming; foolish ones can't see what's right in front of them.

edges.reason: Sets those who know what will be against those who can’t.
edges.quote: know what will be

couplets.gloss: Not being afraid of what deserves fear is stupid: wise people are afraid of what they should be.

edges.reason: Praises the fear that stops you before the danger, not after.
edges.quote: To fear what should be feared is the way of those who understand

edges.reason: Puts not fearing what should be feared down as plain folly.
edges.quote: Not to fear what should be feared is folly

couplets.gloss: Someone who prepares for what might happen won't be shaken when disaster arrives.

edges.reason: Promises those who guard against what is to come that no suffering will shake them.
edges.quote: guard against what is to come

couplets.gloss: Sensible people have everything; those without sense have nothing, whatever they own.

edges.reason: Lets understanding outweigh every possession, and leaves all possessions empty without it.
edges.quote: Those with understanding have everything

couplets.gloss: Someone free of arrogance, rage and lust has a dignity that makes their success look well on them.

edges.reason: Pride is the first of three faults whose absence gives prosperity its greatness.
edges.quote: pride

edges.reason: Named second of the three that must be gone for prosperity to have greatness.
edges.quote: anger

edges.reason: Aiyar's own note reads the vulgar passion as lust, third of the faults.
edges.quote: the vulgar passion

edges.reason: Someone on the rise hears what actually dignifies success: freedom from pride and temper.
edges.quote: a prosperity with greatness in it

couplets.gloss: Stinginess, excessive pride and unseemly self-satisfaction are failings in a ruler.

edges.reason: Lists these failings specifically as faults in a ruler.
edges.quote: are faults in a ruler

edges.reason: First of the ruler’s three faults, the hand that will not open.
edges.quote: Miserliness

edges.reason: His third fault is joy with no measure, being too pleased with how things stand.
edges.quote: joy with no measure

edges.reason: Honour that has lost its nobility is really pride, and it stands second of the three.
edges.quote: honour that has lost its nobility

couplets.gloss: People who care about their good name treat a fault as small as a grain as if it were as big as a tree.

edges.reason: Praises those who take a tiny fault of their own as seriously as a huge one.
edges.quote: as if it were as big as a palmyra tree

edges.reason: A millet seed grows into a palmyra tree in the eyes of those who fear blame.
edges.quote: the size of a millet seed

couplets.gloss: Watch out for your own faults above all, because they are the real enemies that bring you down.

edges.reason: Makes guarding against your own faults the first charge, since they are the real enemy.
edges.quote: Guard against fault as your one aim

couplets.gloss: A person who doesn't prepare before trouble arrives will go up like straw in front of a flame.

edges.reason: Shows the cost of not guarding in advance: sudden and total ruin.
edges.quote: doesn’t guard in advance

edges.reason: Someone unguarded is a stack of straw before a fire.
edges.quote: a stack of straw before a fire

couplets.gloss: If a ruler fixes his own faults before looking at others', what fault could be left in him?

edges.reason: Puts the order of work plainly: one's own faults first, then other people's.
edges.quote: removes his own faults first, and then looks at those of others

edges.reason: Frames this as the safeguard of a ruler, who then has no fault left.
edges.quote: If a ruler removes his own faults first

couplets.gloss: The wealth of a miser who won't spend on what should be spent is destined to be lost, not kept.

edges.reason: Turns thrift against itself: wealth kept from what should be done with it perishes.
edges.quote: It will perish

couplets.gloss: Stinginess can't be counted with ordinary faults: it is in a worse class of its own.

edges.reason: Refuses even to count it with anything else, as a thing apart.
edges.quote: is not to be counted with anything else

couplets.gloss: Never be full of yourself, and never be drawn to actions that do no good.

edges.reason: Forbids admiring yourself at any time.
edges.quote: Never admire yourself

couplets.gloss: If you can keep what you most want hidden from others, your enemies' schemes will get nowhere.

edges.reason: Makes a hidden love the defence that leaves an enemy’s schemes with nothing to work on.
edges.quote: without letting your love be known

ideaLinks.reason: Suffering seizes whoever won’t give up attachment, and it doesn’t let go.
ideaLinks.quote: Suffering holds on and won’t let go

ideaLinks.reason: Each thing you give up ends the pain that came from it.
Those who renounce completely have reached the goal, while the rest stay in the net.
ideaLinks.quote: Those who renounce completely have arrived

ideaLinks.reason: Birth is cut off the moment attachment ends, so it is attachment that keeps births coming.
ideaLinks.quote: The moment attachment ends, birth is cut off

ideaLinks.reason: Holding to the one who has no attachment is how you let go of your own.
ideaLinks.quote: so that you can let go of attachment

ideaLinks.reason: Taking what isn’t real for what is brings a wretched birth.
ideaLinks.quote: A wretched birth comes from the delusion

ideaLinks.reason: Whoever has seen the truth reaches the path that doesn’t come back here.
ideaLinks.quote: reach the path that doesn’t come back here

ideaLinks.reason: Craving is the seed, and birth that never ends is what it yields.
ideaLinks.quote: craving is the seed that yields

ideaLinks.reason: Not being born comes to the one who wants to want nothing.
ideaLinks.quote: That comes from wanting to want nothing

ideaLinks.reason: Wanting truthfulness is how freedom from craving comes.
Only those without craving are without suffering, while for the rest it comes on without end.
ideaLinks.quote: Those without craving have no suffering

ideaLinks.reason: The highest renown anyone can win comes from never lying.
ideaLinks.quote: There is no renown like never lying

ideaLinks.reason: Humble speech is hard to come by without subtle listening.
Understanding is what keeps the mind from going wherever it goes.
ideaLinks.quote: doesn’t let the mind go wherever it goes
